land.text: South Australia, which 'then included the Northern Territory (transferred to the Commonwealth in 1911)'

successors.note: Became a state on 1 January 1901 (Territorial evolution of Australia). The Northern Territory was 'separated from South Australia and transferred to Australian government control' on 1 January 1911 (History of the Northern Territory).

capitals.name: Adelaide
capitals.note: The infobox capital field is empty and the page does not use the word capital; it says 'Light decided that the Adelaide plains were the best location for settlement'. Adelaide as seat of government is the researcher's reading.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 0.74 M km2 by the gazetteer (0.93 M km2 with the 129-132 E strip from 1861, and about 2.3 M km2 with the Northern Territory from 1863). The South Australia page itself gives no boundary and no infobox area ('Not in source').

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern South Australia, about 0.93 M km2. The longitudes are the researcher's reading (the modern WA/SA line is 129 E).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: South Australia plus the Northern Territory, about 2.3 M km2 by the gazetteer, from 6 July 1863 to the colony's end. The History of the Northern Territory page: 'In 1863, the Northern Territory was annexed by South Australia by letters patent'.

region.text: the territory between 132 E and 141 E and south of 26 S, with the Adelaide plains as the settlement

ledger.note: 1836: South Australia is proclaimed at Glenelg (28 December 1836). 'The foundation of South Australia is usually considered to be Governor Hindmarsh's Proclamation of South Australia at Glenelg on 28 December 1836'; 'Letters Patent ... were presented to the government on 19 February 1836'. The land is the Territorial evolution page's: created 'between 132 degrees east and 141 degrees east, and south of 26 degrees south' from New South Wales; the South Australia page itself gives no boundary.

region.text: the portion of New South Wales west of South Australia

ledger.note: 1861: the western boundary moves out to 129 E. 'The portion of New South Wales west of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' by letters patent of 10 October 1861 (act of parliament 22 July 1861). The strip south of 26 S between 129 E and 132 E is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the New South Wales region north of South Australia, 129 E to 138 E: the Northern Territory

ledger.note: 1863: South Australia takes the Northern Territory (6 July 1863): 'The New South Wales region north of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' (the Northern Territory); the History of the Northern Territory page: 'In 1863, the Northern Territory was annexed by South Australia by letters patent'.

region.text: South Australia with the Northern Territory as it stood in 1900

ledger.note: 1901: South Australia federates (1 January 1901): 'On 1 January 1901, these colonies, excepting New Zealand (who chose not to join), became states' of the Commonwealth; the Northern Territory is still part of South Australia until 1 January 1911.

certainty.note: The western, eastern and northern lines are meridians (129, 132, 138, 141 E) and the 26 S parallel written into dated letters patent on the Territorial evolution page; control of the Northern Territory was nominal until the Palmerston (Darwin) settlement of 5 February 1869 (History of the Northern Territory).

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 3 pages used: Colony of South Australia, Territorial evolution of Australia, History of the Northern Territory.
The South Australia page is thin on territory: it gives no boundary, no 1861 or 1863 change, no area and no capital. All boundaries come from the Territorial evolution page. Dates: Letters Patent 19 February 1836 (the page 'Act ... finally ratified' that day), proclamation 28 December 1836, self-government October 1856, first parliament 9 March 1857 (not border events). 'South Australia Act 1834' passed 15 August 1834. The page ends the colony's life at 1901 only in the infobox ('1836-1901'); 1 January 1901 comes from the Territorial evolution page. The Northern Territory's transfer to the Commonwealth (1 January 1911) falls after the colony and is carried by commonwealth-of-australia. Wars: the Australian frontier wars page lists only an 1840 shipwreck-survivor killing at Cape Jaffa for South Australia and says the 'final battles took place in the Northern Territory'; no border moved and no entry was made.
